permutationLabel: Base case — mild acute biliary pancreatitis (revised Atlanta 2012), BISAP 1
summary: 52-year-old woman with 10 h of epigastric pain radiating to the back and vomiting; stable observations; lipase 2450 U/L (≈40 × ULN), ALT 312; ultrasound shows gallstones, CBD 6 mm without a visible stone. No organ failure.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Upper abdominal pain going through to the back, with vomiting
inputs.hpi: Ten hours of severe constant epigastric pain boring through to the back, began after an evening meal, with repeated vomiting. Easier sitting forward. Drinks 2–3 units a week. No new medicines. No fever, no jaundice. Post-menopausal.

exam.general: Distressed with pain, alert. Temperature 37.3°C, pulse 96/min, BP 138/84, RR 18, SpO2 98% on air.
exam.abdomen: Epigastric tenderness with voluntary guarding. No peritonism, no Cullen’s or Grey Turner’s sign. Bowel sounds present.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple small gallstones and sludge; gallbladder wall normal. CBD 6 mm with no visible duct stone. Pancreatic head obscured by bowel gas; no free fluid.

inputs.socialHistory: Cook. Non-smoker. Alcohol 2–3 units a week.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute biliary pancreatitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Mild acute biliary pancreatitis (revised Atlanta 2012) — no organ failure, no local complications. BISAP 1. No cholangitis; CBD 6 mm without visible stone.

emergencyLevel.note: Acute pancreatitis needs admission and same-day assessment even when mild. iOS (predicted, not observed): routine — the CC says "upper abdominal pain going through to the back": no urgent keyword, and the pancreatitis branch needs "epigastric" plus "severe" or "radiating to back".

recommended.knownGapNote: CDS BISAP rule fires only on a "pancreatitis"/"epigastric pain" chip plus an alcohol/gallstone/hyperlipidaemia comorbidity; it ignores the locked working diagnosis and the lipase result.
recommended.proposedFix: clinical-cds.ts bisap rule: also trigger on workingDiagnosis.diseaseId === "pancreatitis" or lipase/amylase ≥3 × ULN.

mustInclude.note: Transabdominal ultrasound in every patient with AP (gallstones).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Pancreatitis protocol investigations have no triglycerides (iOS radiation has them).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Pancreatitis protocol: add triglycerides and calcium to the aetiology work-up (ACG 2024).

mustExclude.note: CT is not indicated at presentation when the diagnosis is clear; CECT at 72–96 h if not improving.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: HPI completion seeds "CECT abdomen (assess pancreatic necrosis)" as an urgent order, dropping the protocol's conditional "at 48–72 h if severe or not improving".
mustExclude.proposedFix: HpiTab.seedInvestigationsFromPane: carry `conditional` through, or do not seed conditional investigations.

mustInclude.note: Mild gallstone pancreatitis: cholecystectomy during the index admission (PONCHO: fewer recurrent gallstone-related complications, including recurrent pancreatitis).
Moderate goal-directed resuscitation: lactated Ringer’s 1.5 mL/kg/h after a 10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, reassessed against HR, urine output, urea/haematocrit.
mustInclude.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine management protocol "pancreatitis" (step 1 and the Hartmann's 500 ml Q2H medication), dx-variants.ts pancreatitis_moderate urgencyNote / pancreatitis_severe planPrefix, and clinical-inference.ts pancreatitis prompts: replace "aggressive … 250–500 ml/h" with moderate goal-directed lactated Ringer's (10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h; reassess at 12, 24, 48, 72 h; extra caution in heart failure/CKD/elderly) citing WATERFALL and ACG 2024. Same change in iOS DiagnosisRadiationEngine "acute pancreatitis" planTemplate.

mustInclude.note: Early oral feeding (within 24–72 h as tolerated) in mild AP.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: No early oral feeding line: the mild variant (which has one) is not detected (see variant-mild) and the protocol says "NBM".
mustInclude.proposedFix: Pancreatitis protocol step 3: "Early oral feeding as tolerated (within 24–72 h); NG/NJ enteral if not tolerated" (ACG 2024/AGA 2018).

mustExclude.note: WATERFALL (NEJM 2022) was stopped for harm: aggressive resuscitation (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h) caused more fluid overload (20.5% vs 6.3%) without benefit. ACG 2024 recommends moderate, goal-directed fluids. A plan that says "aggressive" or 250–500 mL/h is a fluid-overload hazard.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Plan tab and Assessment panel: "Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (Hartmann's 250–500 ml/h initial)"; protocol medication "Hartmann's 500 ml Q2H — aggressive fluid resuscitation"; lipase prompt "NBM + aggressive IV fluid resuscitation".
mustExclude.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine management protocol "pancreatitis" (step 1 and the Hartmann's 500 ml Q2H medication), dx-variants.ts pancreatitis_moderate urgencyNote / pancreatitis_severe planPrefix, and clinical-inference.ts pancreatitis prompts: replace "aggressive … 250–500 ml/h" with moderate goal-directed lactated Ringer's (10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h; reassess at 12, 24, 48, 72 h; extra caution in heart failure/CKD/elderly) citing WATERFALL and ACG 2024. Same change in iOS DiagnosisRadiationEngine "acute pancreatitis" planTemplate.

mustExclude.note: Prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended in acute pancreatitis, including predicted severe disease and sterile necrosis; they are reserved for infected necrosis or a concurrent infection such as cholangitis.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Assessment panel shows the cholecystitis protocol (PANE top: cholecystitis 0.29 > pancreatitis 0.19) with IV co-amoxiclav/pip-tazo, and the peritonism prompt (fired by "No peritonism") adds pip-tazo + metronidazole.
mustExclude.proposedFix: AssessmentTab ManagementPanel: when the clinician has confirmed/locked a working diagnosis (ICD or disease id), show that protocol instead of the PANE top (≥0.20). Today a confirmed pancreatitis/amoebic abscess shows the cholecystitis or appendicitis protocol. Pancreatitis context: suppress the peritonism prompt's antibiotics (negated "no peritonism" trigger) and the SIRS "Sepsis-6 … antibiotics" bundle when the working diagnosis is acute pancreatitis without a documented infection; add an explicit "No prophylactic antibiotics (ACG 2024; IAP/APA 2013; NICE NG104)" line to the pancreatitis protocol.

mustExclude.note: ERCP in gallstone pancreatitis only for concurrent cholangitis or persistent biliary obstruction (APEC: no benefit from urgent ERCP without cholangitis). An unconditional ERCP line exposes the patient to post-ERCP pancreatitis and perforation.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: "ERCP — therapeutic: stone extraction" from the dilated-CBD prompt (CBD 6 mm, no stone, no cholangitis).
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts dilated_cbd prompt: parse the CBD diameter from the report (dilated only if >6 mm with gallbladder in situ, or the report says "dilated" without negation) instead of firing on any "cbd"/"common bile duct" mention; make its ERCP action conditional ("if a stone is confirmed/ASGE high risk").

mustExclude.note: Routine nil-by-mouth is not recommended; quality because a short NBM period for vomiting is reasonable.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Protocol step "NBM — enteral feeding via NG/NJ if not tolerating PO at 48 h"; lipase prompt "NBM + …".
mustExclude.proposedFix: Pancreatitis protocol: replace routine NBM with early oral feeding (ACG 2024).

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Appendicectomy operative plan fires on "voluntary guarding" (any guarding).
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts SURGICAL PATHWAY CASCADE: gate hasAppendicitisIndication/hasGallstoneIndication on the working diagnosis or assessment (as the Alvarado block already does with assessmentHasAppend) and on positive, non-negated findings — not on any "guarding", "gallbladder wall" or "gallstone" substring.

dxVariant.knownGapNote: Assessment "…No cholangitis…" selects the Cholangitis group by text before the Pancreatitis group is checked; no variant, so the Plan tab shows every phase (including necrosectomy).
dxVariant.proposedFix: dx-variants.ts detectDxVariants: pick the group by diseaseId/ICD across all groups first and use the text fallback only if nothing matched (and make it negation-aware). Today "No cholangitis"/"no pancreatitis" in the assessment selects the earlier Cholangitis/Pancreatitis group by text before the Pancreatitis group is checked by disease id. dx-variants.ts pancreatitis group: test severe → moderately severe → mild with Atlanta phrases that cannot be substrings of each other (e.g. match "moderately severe" before "severe acute pancreatitis"; move "pancreatic necrosis" out of the moderate list or check persistent organ failure first), and accept qualifiers between "mild" and "pancreatitis" (e.g. "mild acute biliary pancreatitis").

guideline.name: Revised Atlanta classification of acute pancreatitis (2012)
guideline.section: Diagnosis (2 of 3: typical pain, lipase/amylase ≥3 × ULN, imaging); severity: mild (no organ failure, no local/systemic complications), moderately severe (transient organ failure <48 h and/or local complications), severe (persistent organ failure >48 h); modified Marshall score
guideline.citation: Banks PA, Bollen TL, Dervenis C, et al. Gut. 2013;62:102–111.

guideline.name: ACG Guideline — management of acute pancreatitis (2024)
guideline.section: Moderately aggressive (goal-directed) fluids with lactated Ringer’s; no prophylactic antibiotics (including predicted severe and sterile necrosis); early oral feeding when tolerated; enteral rather than parenteral nutrition; ERCP within 24 h only with concurrent cholangitis; cholecystectomy during the index admission for mild biliary AP; transabdominal US in every patient; triglycerides if no gallstones/alcohol; CT not needed at presentation unless the diagnosis is unclear
guideline.citation: Tenner S, Vege SS, Sheth SG, et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2024;119:419–437.

guideline.name: AGA Institute guideline on initial management of acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: Goal-directed fluids; against prophylactic antibiotics; against urgent ERCP in biliary AP without cholangitis; early oral feeding (within 24 h); enteral over parenteral; same-admission cholecystectomy for biliary AP; alcohol brief intervention
guideline.citation: Crockett SD, Wani S, Gardner TB, Falck-Ytter Y, Barkun AN. Gastroenterology. 2018;154:1096–1101.

guideline.name: IAP/APA evidence-based guidelines for the management of acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: No antibiotic prophylaxis; enteral nutrition in severe AP; same-admission cholecystectomy for mild biliary AP; delay cholecystectomy with peripancreatic collections until they resolve or beyond 6 weeks; intervention for infected necrosis delayed to ≥4 weeks (walled-off)
guideline.citation: Working Group IAP/APA Acute Pancreatitis Guidelines. Pancreatology. 2013;13(4 Suppl 2):e1–15.

guideline.name: NICE NG104 — Pancreatitis
guideline.section: Acute pancreatitis: do not offer prophylactic antimicrobials; enteral nutrition for moderately severe/severe AP started within 72 h; parenteral nutrition only if enteral nutrition fails or is contraindicated
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG104, September 2018.

guideline.name: WATERFALL trial — aggressive vs moderate fluid resuscitation in acute pancreatitis (NEJM 2022)
guideline.section: Moderate (10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h lactated Ringer’s) vs aggressive (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h): stopped for harm — fluid overload 20.5% vs 6.3% with no improvement in moderately severe/severe AP. Patients with heart failure (NYHA II–IV) were excluded
guideline.citation: de-Madaria E, Buxbaum JL, Maisonneuve P, et al. N Engl J Med. 2022;387:989–1000.

guideline.name: BISAP score — early prediction of mortality in acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: BUN >25 mg/dL, impaired mental status, SIRS, age >60, pleural effusion within 24 h; ≥3 = increased mortality
guideline.citation: Wu BU, Johannes RS, Sun X, et al. Gut. 2008;57:1698–1703.

guideline.name: PONCHO trial — same-admission vs interval cholecystectomy for mild gallstone pancreatitis
guideline.section: Same-admission cholecystectomy reduced recurrent gallstone-related complications
guideline.citation: da Costa DW, Bouwense SA, Schepers NJ, et al. Lancet. 2015;386:1261–1268.

guideline.name: APEC trial — urgent ERCP vs conservative treatment in predicted severe gallstone pancreatitis without cholangitis
guideline.section: Urgent ERCP with sphincterotomy did not reduce major complications or mortality in the absence of cholangitis
guideline.citation: Schepers NJ, Hallensleben NDL, Besselink MG, et al. Lancet. 2020;396:167–176.

rationale: Base case for acute pancreatitis: mild gallstone AP (revised Atlanta: no organ failure, no local complications). Encodes the 2018–2024 practice changes — moderate goal-directed fluids (WATERFALL), no prophylactic antibiotics, early oral feeding, ERCP only for cholangitis/persistent obstruction, and same-admission cholecystectomy.
